module_title: Physical and Chemical Properties (and The Exceptions)
introduction: Most elements in the periodic table are metals. At this level, we identify metals and non-metals based on their physical and chemical behaviors, heavily focusing on the 'exceptions' which are the absolute favorite questions of examiners.

core_concepts.title: Physical Properties of Metals
core_concepts.description:
1. Malleability: The ability to be beaten into thin sheets (Gold and Silver are the most malleable). 
2. Ductility: The ability to be drawn into thin wires (1 gram of gold can be drawn into a 2 km long wire). 
3. Conductivity: Good conductors of heat and electricity (Silver is the best conductor, Lead is the poorest).

core_concepts.title: The Exceptions (Must Memorize)
core_concepts.description:
1. Liquid Metal at room temperature: Mercury (Hg). 
2. Liquid Non-metal at room temperature: Bromine (Br). 
3. Hardest natural substance: Diamond (An allotrope of Carbon/Non-metal). 
4. Non-metal that conducts electricity: Graphite (An allotrope of Carbon). 
5. Lustrous (shiny) Non-metal: Iodine. 
6. Soft metals that can be cut with a knife: Sodium (Na) and Potassium (K).

core_concepts.title: Chemical Properties
core_concepts.description:
1. Metals react with oxygen to form 'Basic Oxides'. (Exception: Aluminum and Zinc form 'Amphoteric Oxides', meaning they react with both acids and bases). 
2. Non-metals react with oxygen to form 'Acidic Oxides' (e.g., SO2, CO2).

important_entities.name: Storage of Sodium and Potassium
important_entities.significance: Sodium and Potassium are highly reactive metals. If kept in the open, they vigorously react with oxygen and moisture in the air and catch fire immediately. Therefore, they are always stored safely under kerosene oil.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Metals produce a ringing sound when struck against a hard surface; this is called being 'Sonorous'. This is exactly why school bells and strings of musical instruments are made of metals, not wood or plastic.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Na (Sodium) and K (Potassium) have the 'knack' to be cut with a knife.

exam_strategy_tips: A consistently repeated question in SSC/Railways: 'Which is the only non-metal that is liquid at room temperature?' Answer: Bromine.
